newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN JULY GOLD IMPORTS RISE 319 PCT YR/YR.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN JULY GOLD IMPORTS RISE 319 PCT YR/YR.

text.p: Taiwan's imports of gold bars, coins and plate in July rose 319 percent to 14.611 tonnes compared to 4.582 tonnes in July 1996, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.

Traders said sharply lower world gold prices and Taiwan's rallying stock market were the main factors prompting the big year on year import spurt, explaining that local demand for jewellery was very strong.
"Gold prices are still low and many people are buying gold jewellery with money they've made in the stock market," a gold retailer said.
Taiwan's main stock index has roughly doubled in value since the first half of 1996.
Traders said the jewellery industry had increased its July imports in anticipation of strong retail sales ahead of the traditional Chinese Lover's Day holiday, which this year falls on August 9.
The ministry said Taiwan's gold exports in July remained modest at 0.185 tonnes, down 15.5 percent compared to the 0.219 tonnes exported in July 1996.
